summary:
He shouldn’t have done it.Sleeping with his king — in the state Arthur was in that night.The worst part is, he doesn’t even remember all of it.— Just enough.
The kiss. Arthur’s mouth, warm against his own. The breathless moans pulled from his throat. The way it felt like he was drunk — but even without the potion that caused all of this, Merlin knew one touch from Arthur would make him feel like he'd spent two whole weeks drinking in the tavern.
And flashes of what came next.Enough to know that this time, he truly fucked up.So when he wakes, naked in his king’s bed, Merlin does the only thing he can — he grabs his clothes and runs.He barely makes it to Gaius’s chambers, disheveled and panicked, only to find the old man already holding the book Merlin now realizes — far too late — he mistranslated.And in that moment, it hits him. There is no undoing this.
“Merlin,” Gaius says, voice low “pack your things. Go as far away as you can."“You’re carrying His Majesty’s child.”
Or
Arthur was being too much, and Merlin—a clumsy fool—mistranslated an ancient text and brewed a potion meant to calm His Majesty, only to end up pregnant with the king’s child instead.

“Of whoring?”

summary: Fifteen hundred years. I’m sure it’s been fifteen hundred years because I’ve felt every single moment of it. Every draw of breath, every step on the hard ground, every ounce of stark reality has been obvious to me. I’m not the same as I was. Time has a way of digging deep into your spirit and settling its claws there. And I will wait. I have no choice, but I keep telling myself that wouldn’t matter. It might not matter. Would he even know me? Behind this familiar face is a creature who has lived the lives of hundreds of tortured souls. Does it show? Could he see the desperation there? If I made him look, really look...If he were here, I like to think I could be who I once was. Could feel the release of the claws of time like a weight coming off my chest. summary:
Merlin’s mother had made it very clear to him what he should do when she sent him off to Camelot. Merlin wasn’t to tell anyone he had magic, his mother was scared that he would be collared to keep him in line if someone found out. Yet, Camelot was, above all, one of the best places for an alpha warlock to be. In Essitir, the omega king would drag alphas off to his palace once they were old enough, claim them, and use them for their powers. It was a fate that Merlin’s mother had feared him facing since he presented at twelve summers old. It was why, on the eve of his eighteenth summer, she sent him away to the bordering kingdom before Cenred’s men could show up in Elador to take him away. In Camelot Merlin could have a future. 
It was a more hopeful future than what he would have in any other kingdom.
Other than Essitir and Camelot, all other kingdoms executed alphas who had magic, mated or not, too afraid of what they could do. Camelot had done the same, once, but that had changed when the Queen had fallen for an alpha sorceress and had taken her as her mate, changing the law to allow mated magical alphas to live in peace. 
All Merlin had to do was catch an omega....

We’re…” his voice trailed out as he glanced to Merlin, faltering.  They exchanged a look which Leon could not understand, before Arthur turned back to him.  “Merlin, tell Leon what we’re doing.”“We’re…” Merlin looked to Arthur, and it was obvious from his expression that he was at a loss, however it was only momentary.  When he turned back to Leon, his face had changed; it had grown resolute, decided.  “I’m teaching him some poetry.”

title: Do you love him?
author: NotoriousJYT
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
relationships: Other Relationship Tags to Be Added
summary:
"Do you love him?”
Queen Ygraine asks the question gently, but Arthur knows better than to mistake gentleness for mercy.
He has come to ask permission to formally court Merlin: son of Balinor, Chief Dragonlord of Albion, and Hunith, Ygraine’s trusted lady-in-waiting. It should be simple. It is not.
Because Merlin is not only the man Arthur loves. He is Dragonkind’s future, Dafyd’s blood, Druid-touched magic, and a sovereignty older than Pendragon law.
In a Camelot where Ygraine survived and magic returned to public life, Albion has rebuilt itself around a fragile peace between Crown, Dragonkind, the Old Religion, and the old threshold kingdoms. But restoration is not the same as healing.
As Arthur and Merlin’s courtship becomes public, Ascetir’s roots begin to stir, Dafyd’s tidal arches hum at the wrong tide, Avalon’s mists remember what Camelot forgot, and old roads bend toward the Forest of Balor and the Great Stones of Nemeton.
Something wounded beneath Albion has begun to ask for witness.
Or: Ygraine lives, Arthur loves Merlin openly, and Albion discovers that love is not weakness, possession, or conquest — but covenant.

For years, he carved lines into the earth and runes into his own skin. Now, it is time to crack both open and drag the future back to his King. But, as warned in the days of old, nothing is brought back without a cost.
He is a king-maker who has outlived his sovereign; a warlock who has finally stopped bartering with words and started bartering with existence. He will pay any price if it means his heart never goes where he cannot follow him again.
Merlin burrows to a past that hasn't yet bled, and is no longer the bumbling servant Camelot remembers. He is something older, hungrier, and powerful beyond measure. This time, Arthur will not just wear a crown; Merlin will carve him into a god to match his own dark divinity. And if it takes a little blood to bind them together, to ensure what he is owed, who he earned, then Merlin will gladly teach his prince how to thirst for it.

title: Destiny Defied
author: Neverendedforme
summary: Camelot has no king. All that remains is Queen Guinevere and Sir Leon. His steady friendship is all she has left, offering her a hint of... love? Then Merlin turns up—he didn't die as feared and has returned. Instead of joy at his return, Gwen is angry. She assumed him dead—now it seems he abandoned her. Merlin never meant to leave her, he needed time, but it seems she can't see it as anything else. No matter how hard he tries, he isn't enough—maybe Gwen needs something else. Someone else. Can he resurrect the past for her—or should the past stay in the past? As if tensions in Camelot aren't enough, a seemingly trivial error has morphed into a threat lurking outside the kingdom. Time reveals the threat is already within the castle—close to the queen. It seems the past can't let go of Camelot, and with the Cup of Life falling into the conflict, past mixes with future. Camelot needs a new start. The old ways versus the new. Fear. Respect. Magic. Fear alone can't lead Camelot, respect must be earned and magic's future is uncertain.They'd all begun to think they were safe—but is Camelot even meant to have a future? Or is it doomed to the destiny of its past kings? To die—and leave them all devastated amidst its ashes.

As a child, Arthur didn’t know why he was kept away from the courtyard.
Or why it so often smelt… like that.
Until one morning, Sir Kay guided him to the balcony he’d only been allowed on sometimes. Only sometimes, because it looks over the courtyard.
His father was waiting for him, holding an arm out to beckon him closer. Arthur rushed in, latching himself onto his father’s side as it was so rarely permitted.
There was a crowd below him; he had never seen so many people in one place.
There was a pile of wood.
He remembers little outside of the way his eyes burned, how he at last understood that smell. He remembers forcing down his supper that night and emptying his stomach in the corridor before he could even reach his room.
Now he remembers it all.
He can’t feel the bruising stones under his knees, hardly tastes the leftover bile coating his mouth.
All he knows is the all-consuming realization that his greatest fear and anguish still holds the throne, even in his heart.

title: A Servant's Friendship

summary:
Lynette cared for magic but could never wield such wonder except in her dreams. As the physician's daughter, many people would find her helping the elderly with their large loads or playing with the children in alleyways. As a humble servant to her thriving kingdom, Lynette struggles to face the light of a new dawn in the war against magic. A light that manifests in her long-predestined fate as the one they call the once and future queen.
Arthur feared magic and all it had taken and could take from him. As the son of a king, most would find him training with his knights or at his desk with mounds of paperwork. As the kingdom's prince, Arthur held on to every moment of freedom until it was his time to rule. A luxury that would fade into darkness and give way to his fate as the once and future king.
Magic knew no bounds when it came to the constraints of destiny. It tended to morph and evolve until it was unrecognizable to all except those who knew it. An untamable force that struck fear into the hearts of many and yet longing in others. A destiny that weaves a sorcerer, servant, and prince into a chain of unpredictable events that would go down in history as legends in the Albion escapades.

The man was beautiful. Hair as gold as dawn sunlight, eyes like the endless blue depths of a midsummer afternoon. His face was a marble angel’s, the lines of brow and cheek and jaw almost too mathematically perfect. Every good sculptor always knew to put in a flaw. His was in his front teeth, just a little too large, and it made Merlin dig his fingernails into his palms. He was lithe, muscular, dressed in black. Half-dressed - his jerkin was unbuttoned, his shirt open nearly to his navel, and he was missing a sock. His hair had the raked-through look of a man in crisis. His smile was dazzling and mad.
“This,” he said, spreading his hands, “is the magnificent - nay, the opulent court of the Crown Prince of Camelot!”
And then, very pleasantly - “Gaius, what the fuck is this?”

title: Unraveling
author: Fuck_Right_Off

summary:
Sir Leon was making a joke—or perhaps a mockery of him. George is unsure now, but the servant did not take it as such, and the servant responded incorrectly. He fears he might have been the butt of this particular joke. 
“I cannot sleep when things are disorderly. I need things to be as I left them.” George explains anyway—as if maybe that would ease the pressure in his chest. To voice it. To make it known. This is not a matter of want, it's a need. Everything has felt in disarray. Nothing is exactly as it was before. George will not be able to let this go. He will not be able to sleep. 
But Sir Leon laughs again—more instinctive than anything—he is not as aware as he usually is. George usually appreciates how tidy Sir Leon keeps his room—he enjoys being in his room the most. But in this particular moment, he does not. It feels small now. He feels small. Everything is a mess. 
“I was not making a joke, sire,” George speaks—his voice on the edge of something. He did not like being laughed at. Especially not by Sir Leon. 
---or---

title: He did not live in Ealdor anymore
author: gloriask
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
When you ask what Magic was to Merlin. It was the way his hoe broke the spring earth without his hands aching by sundown, the way the well-bucket rose at the curl of his fingers. It was a hearth-fire coaxed from damp wood when the cold months grew long. The seam in Will's boot that closed itself. It was the spell Merlin whispered into his own straw mattress, soft, soft, until the ticking grew tender as wool.
Back then in Ealdor, Merlin had never thought his magic would kill people.
He did not live in Ealdor anymore.

The last warlock. 
The last true caster of magic. 
The last god. 
The last dragonkin.

summary: Destiny plays a cruel game with us. It lets us hope, lets us believe we are in control, just for things to end the way we knew they would anyways. But sometimes, to it’s very favorites, destiny will be kind. One of those favorites is Merlin. And what if this time it will actually end differently? What if this time he would find a way to show Morgana that violence was not the only option? What if this time, he could help Mordred not loose his loyalty. What if this time he could be honest with this man earlier on? Share his secret with him and show what magic can also be. Show him the beauty and peace it can bring. And what if this time he could build the courage to tell Arthur how he truly felt, before it will be too late again? If he could do all those things, could the ending truly be changed? Could he watch Arthur be the king he was destined to be instead of watching the love of his life die in his arms without him ever truly knowing what he meant for the young warlock? Merlin wasn’t sure. Anything he had ever done to try and change the cause of events had led to the exact situations he tried to avoid. But if destiny gives you a chance like this, you use it. His partner reassures him that he doesn’t have to carry everything alone or be perfect all the time. summary:
Arthur Pendragon walked through history with fire trailing in his wake. That was the hand that had carved Bayard of Mercia open and left him to die for six days pinned upon his desecrated throne. Those were the eyes that had looked down from the peaks of Mount Wyddfa and seen nothing below him that he could not conquer. The songs called him siegebreaker, earthshaker, battle-ender. Arthur Pendragon, deified and awful, protected by some great work of magic forged at his birth. Arthur Pendragon, whom no weapon forged by man could kill.
He had a nice smile. That was the first thing that struck Merlin. All the songs called him handsome, and Merlin could attest to their truth - those ice-blue eyes, that golden hair, that face carved as if from marble. He’d been prepared for that beauty, steeled against it. But he had not been prepared for that smile. It was an amused look, yes, but not coldly distant. It welcomed. It invited shared laughter, understanding, perhaps even the promise of brotherhood. For a second, Merlin could understand why so many men would follow the prince to their deaths.

George has heard the man throw commands to his troops—has heard him say long, profound speeches to the court. He is a very intelligent man. Yet—standing in the middle of the head servants' quarters—in full armor, he stands mute.
A servant is not to speak unless spoken to.
Sir Leon looks…hesitant to speak. Perhaps it is something of a delicate nature.
“Sire?” George begins. “Is there something you require of me?”
—or—-
George and Leon have been unconventional friends for years. They’ve been in love for just as long.

summary:
Merlin - raised by the druids - was taught that his destiny is for Arthur Pendragon to die at his hands, and that would end the Great Purge. It was Emrys who would restore magic to the lands, following the burial of the Pendragon dynasty.
One day, the druids Merlin had grew up with had stained their hands with something similar to Emrys’s sins - they had captured a small group of passer-byers that posed a threat. Two knights from Camelot were among the four.
Emrys had the displeasure of dealing with the intruders first, having to intimidate them until someone with higher authority would decide whether killing them would secure their safety.
Unfortunately, Merlin had always been a curious boy.
He has yet to discover that trying to be anything more than a murderer to these men would be where he met destiny. He was talking with the reason he was born.
What happens when he betrays everything he’s learned just to hope that this prince would reach out over a chance to love? What happens when he binds himself to Arthur using magic?

tags: Arthur Pendragon Finds Out About Merlin's Magic (Merlin)
summary:
With King Uther’s health rapidly deteriorating, Arthur Pendragon must do what all kings before him have done: go on a quest to prove himself the next worthy leader of Camelot. But when his quest leads him to a mysterious tower with a rumored dark past, Arthur begins to question the things he’s been told.
There are stories about what lurks in the tower outside of Gorra. Some say it is the wellspring of evil itself; the beating heart of all magic. Others claim to have glimpsed a twisted creature through its single dirty window. They say whatever lives there is cursed—trapped forever in a labyrinth of rooms, and if you go in, you don’t come out. Nobody ever comes out.
Arthur is sure they’re all old wives’ tales. The building is clearly abandoned, after all. But as Arthur delves further into the tower’s past, nothing is quite as it seems. Is this place truly home to a monster, or is there something else afoot? And who is the mysterious man who wanders its halls?

Alexander is 17 years old, born to an English father and Italian mother. He is a creative soul

lonely and undesired due to his family's abusive behavior and his friends' incapability to
understand him.

Quixote, the Mad Hatter and King Arthur. Here, Alex's inner demons – his loneliness, his

world and the pages of his diary, Alex must learn to overcome his fears and finally slay the
beast.

summary:
“I believe it,” Arthur sighs, “I won’t ever get a break, will I? How is it I’ve managed to become the sole entertainment for two sorcerers? I mean, really.” 
Merlin chuckles, “I think his magic just… recognizes you.” 
Merlin can hear Arthur's breath stutter behind him. “Oh, that’s…” 
“I know,” he agrees, turning in Arthur’s arms so he can finally see his face. In the moonlight Arthur appears quite taken, the sudden pull of emotion heavy in the blue of his eyes as he stares back at Merlin unblinking. “I keep thinking about what my mother said. How she thinks his magic is just acting out because he doesn’t know what it’s like to be afraid of showing it. How he feels safe. With you.” 
Arthur’s jaw tightens and finally he does look away, something glistening in his eyes as he loosens his hold on Merlin’s waist. 
“With you too,” he mumbles, blinking just a little too quickly, “...maybe we are doing something right.” 
 
-

In a land of myth and a time of magic, the fate of the world rests on the shoulders of one man, his name… Merlin. Or so the tales go. But tales have a way of getting away from oneself, and history has a way of morphing. For while the fate of the world would always rest on Merlin’s shoulders, how he determined that fate had a way of changing, of spinning out, from one tale to another, from one moment to the next, in a web of different destinies. For this tale has been told before, and shall be again, in a web of magic and time, in choice and fate, in friendship and family, and in love and duty. With the simple act of a single man leaving something as small and insignificant as a mere cloak behind, so our tale begins.
When Merlin uses his father's crest to get Lancelot into the knights it's sets off a series of events that change the future of Camelot and Albion forever. Can Merlin make it through his time as Arthur's squire alive? Can he protect his new found family while hiding his growing feelings for his prince? Can Arthur hide his for his manservant turned squire? Only time will tell.

Maybe The World's Only Novel About The Blob
summary:
Fred Dukes was always the joke.
The Blob. A 700-pound caricature of mass and menace—forever the punching bag, the obstacle, the comic relief. A towering freak for the X-Men to overcome on their way to grander battles and nobler causes.
But once, in a fleeting false utopia, Fred glimpsed something different. Dignity. Intelligence. Maybe even love. Then the dream shattered—as utopias do—and he tried to live quietly in the wreckage. No more tights. No more teams. Just peace.
Villainy had other plans. It doesn't let go of its favorite sons so easily.
One catastrophe later, Fred finds himself marooned in a very different Avalon—alongside Elizabeth Braddock, the razor-sharp Captain Britain, and Doctor Stephen Strange, the smug Sorcerer Supreme.
Avalon is a land of wonder and mysteries. A place where magic has rules… and mass has power.
And when Fred Dukes puts on a wizard hat and declares himself the Muscle Wizard, those rules break.
But the higher you rise in Avalon, the harder it bites back.

Opportunity falls into his lap when police detective Arthur Pendragon attempts to recruit him as a special expert on Camelot’s Magicside for the investigation. Apparently, Arthur also believes Emrys is being framed.
Of course, there is the issue that Arthur's father is the reason Merlin's father is in prison, falsely accused of murder.
And that Arthur is a prat, if a ridiculously handsome one.
But working with him seems a small price to pay for access to any information the police might have on the case. And Merlin knows Arthur is different from his father.
As the two men work together, they find themselves falling for each other. But can that work out, considering all that stands between them? And can they find the murderer before they kill again?

summary:
Sir Thomas had taken a step forward and before he knew it, Merlin was face first in the dirt, one arm twisted cruelly behind him and held down by a knee to the centre of his back. Merlin’s head was spinning, and his cheek—where it was shoved into the solid ground—was throbbing painfully. He swallowed thickly and held back the groan of pain that collected at the back of his throat.
 
“Haven’t you heard, mutt? Servants should be seen and not heard,” Sir Thomas whispered, lowering Merlin’s arm and placing it almost delicately on the ground. Merlin made a move to push himself up, but Thomas’ grip only tightened, holding Merlin’s arm flat on the ground, his knee still jammed into his back. “Now, I think I’m going to teach you a lesson. You’re going to learn to hold that tongue of yours before I cut it out myself, do I make myself clear?”

Between the Cailleach—who watched him silently—and the swirling darkness of the rend in the fabric of the world, sat a squat circle of stones, built up into a small wall. A well. Either Merlin had not noticed it before or, more likely, it had materialised before him without his notice. He could feel how alive this place was with magic, though none of it felt quite right at the gateway that should never have been. The hairs on the back of his neck raised, as if something had breathed down it, and Merlin shivered.
It was now or never.
Merlin perched himself on the edge of the wall, swinging his legs round until they dangled into nothingness. With one final glance at the men who still argued, each one of them dear to him, he caught Arthur’s eyes at last. Merlin’s heart sank in his chest, as he watched Arthur’s jaw drop.

summary: It was when Merlin was peeking over the edge of his glass with a dumbstruck look on his face that Arthur finally saw him. The second their eyes met a cold shock ran through him, petrifying and powerful. He took the first breath he could remember since so long ago. It was like he had been splashed with water, finally waking from an uncanny dream. His eyes locked on blue and suddenly time made sense again. Then those heavenly eyes continued their path, not hesitating for even a breath, and some part of Merlin broke. Arthur didn’t recognize him. Of course he didn’t. This wasn’t the Arthur that he used to know. He was someone who was born into this modern life, growing and learning separately to Merlin. There wasn’t anything that they shared together anymore. ---“God, I despise it but… there is something about you.”“It’s been said before.” By you. And now Merlin got to hear it again, along with every other stupid comment and ingenuous insult that Arthur was always so fond of making. They got to be together again. Even if they had to start from the beginning. Even if he wasn’t the one he’d lost. Merlin got to have him back.

title: so cold then so sweet
author: lemonlesbian
tags: Arthur Pendragon Can’t Live Without Merlin
summary:
Merlin wakes to the sound of his wooden, frail bedroom door creaking open. Through his tired eyes he watches a figure slip past the threshold–familiar but worrying for this isn’t something that they have done before–and shut the door with a gentle click, so as to not wake his mentor on the other side of it.
“Arthur?” Merlin sits up in his bed, his thin blanket pooling around his waist. The moon shines in from the small window near the ceiling, helping the adjustment of his vision to the darkness. He hopes the redness leftover from his earlier crying isn’t obvious with the streak of moonlight entering through his window. “What are you doing here? Is something the matter?”
“No,” Arthur answers, voice wavering on something that tells Merlin the opposite, “nothing important.”
Merlin frowns. Because yes, it is important if it’s the reason for his weighed down shoulders, the furrow on his forehead, the vulnerability shining through his distant eyes.

If you were to ask Merlin to count how many times Arthur Pendragon had died in his arms, he would look at you as if you knew the secrets of the world. “Twenty four,” he would solemnly say. “I happen to be exceptionally skilled at letting him die.” You would nod your head, say: “I understand, it’s not your fault,” and he would look at you with so much confusion you can’t help but laugh. “Who are you?” he would say then, and you would stop laughing immediately. Because what would you say?  That you were the reason this was happening to him? That you were the reason he was losing his mind? That you were the land itself? Because they were all true. And they had surrounded him.

Arthur has always known that Merlin is keeping secrets.
He has known it when Merlin stood up to him in a marketplace, eyes full of defiance and not a shred of fear to be found. He has known it when Merlin swung a mace at him even though it was clear that he had never handled one before, refusing to cower before anyone, prince or not. He has known it when Uther had made Merlin his servant, and Merlin looked as if he would walk out of Camelot right then and there.

Sometimes, you love despite, not because. Sometimes, finding out does not change anything.

title: The Tale of Calibor.
author: greek_in_nature
tags: References to Ancient Celtic Religions & Lore
summary:
This tale took place hundreds of years ago in the time of heroes, dragons, and grand impossible quests. It is already over before the first page is begun. It has already reached its conclusion. It was always going to turn out this way. Those who will die have been dead since the beginning; there is nothing you or I can do to change it. We are merely spectators to a story that cannot be swayed.
This tale may be over but it is also happening right now, right here, as your eyes skim these words. It will continue to repeat itself and I will continue to tell it. The people in this tale have done all of this before and will do it again and again until time ceases to exist.
This is how a man becomes a sword, how a prince becomes a king, and how a servant becomes a sorcerer. This is how a kingdom ascends and crumbles. This is how fire spreads.
The prelude of the end begins now.

“Morgana, what—?”

tags: Arthur Pendragon Finds Out About Merlin's Magic (Merlin)
summary:
Before Merlin's hand could even fall, Arthur stood in front of him, fury, disgust and pain in his eyes as he held the blood soaked dagger from the deer against Merlin's throat.
The Warlock froze. "Oh," he whispered, shocked. "I- I didn't-"
Arthur's jaw clenched. "Didn't what, sorcerer. Didn't think I'd catch you? How long? How long have you been plotting?" He snapped and Merlin frowned, still shellshocked.
"Didn't think you- you would actually kill me," he murmured, Arthur faltering as Merlin stared at the red staining Arthur's forearms with a shaky smile.
~~~~

title: King Emrys of Oplaria
author: ilikereadingig
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
relationships: Knights of the Round Table & Merlin (Merlin)
tags: The Knights Know About Merlin's Magic (Merlin)
summary:
Merlin follows Arthur on his quest to the Perilous lands, returning not just with his friend alive and well but also a new kingdom. Magic has lost so much from the purge and the years after and the first rule of magic is that there must be balance, so it gives back. Creating the Kingdom of Oplaria, ruled by King Emrys.
But Merlin is not so keen to abandon his destiny and Arthur, he spends his time between the two Kingdoms constantly torn between his friendship with Arthur and his duty to his people and magic. He is good at secret identities after all.
But with Arthur constantly sidelining Merlin how long can he make excuses to stay?And how much will this change not only the Prophecy but also the future of Albion?
This follows the show from Season 3 episode 8 -> Season 4 episode 13, then abandons cannon all together, but will include storylines from other episodes.
If like me you loved all the side characters well then get ready to get a lot more time with them (especially if you love Mithian, Elena and Vivian).
Or,
Basically "Deliver Us" from the Prince of Egypt and Merlin being Daenerys Targaryen
